title: R.S. Joshi v. Ajit Mills Ltd.

content.caseIdentity: R.S. Joshi v. Ajit Mills Ltd., (1977) 4 SCC 98
content.holding: Colourable legislation is a phrase denoting lack of legislative power masked by form; courts cannot strike down competent laws on allegations of improper legislative motives.
content.relevance: Reaffirmation of strict competence test over legislative ethics.

evidence.note: Supreme Court of India (1977) 4 SCC 98; 1977 INSC 165; 1978 (1) SCR 338; 7-Judge Constitution Bench on colourable legislation and incidental powers.
